actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.name: ticks

device.name: CRL Humanoid ROS Unitree G1 (MuJoCo scene)

facts.text: The repository is a ROS 2 framework for humanoid robot simulation and control that supports the Unitree G1 and LimX Tron1A platforms.
The repository lists MuJoCo-based software-in-the-loop testing as its simulation role.
The card's first model is the MJCF scene 'g1 scene crl', which includes g1_29dof_crl.xml.
The robot model compiles angles in radians and resolves its meshes from meshes/.
The pelvis body is placed at 0 0 0.793 and carries the free joint floating_base_joint.
The left hip pitch joint declares range -2.5307 2.8798 and actuatorfrcrange -88 88.
The actuator block has 29 motor actuators, one for each leg, waist and arm joint, and none sets ctrlrange or ctrllimited.
The model declares gyro and accelerometer sensors for the torso and pelvis IMUs.
The scene's worldbody adds a directional light and a plane geom named floor.
The G1 simulator declares robot_xml_file with the default g1_description/scene_crl.xml.
initializeMuJoCo loads the robot_xml_file model with mj_loadXML and sets the model option timestep to timeStepSize_.
BaseNode declares the time_step_size parameter with default 0.01 and stores it in timeStepSize_.
The G1 simulator configuration sets the robot node's time_step_size to 0.001667.
The repository's crl_humanoid_hardware G1Node names the Unitree SDK2 low-level command and state topics rt/lowcmd and rt/lowstate for the 29 G1 motors.
The README lists MuJoCo 3.3.5 as the simulation dependency.

determinism.notes: The stand-in integrates the same placeholder response for the same controls from the model defaults; it has no seed input and its motion is not MuJoCo's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the card's scene and its include for the free base, the 29 hinge joints, the 29 motor channels and the model option timestep, then integrates a placeholder torque response and joint motion

the stand-in computes no inertia, mass matrix, gravity, contact, friction, equality, tendon or actuator dynamics, loads no STL mesh or texture, and does not implement MuJoCo's integration-state snapshot API; a fake trajectory is not a MuJoCo trajectory
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine or with the upstream ROS simulator

the G1 MJCF sets no option timestep, so a direct load runs at the engine's library default (the stand-in uses 2 ms); the upstream ROS simulator instead sets the model timestep from its time_step_size parameter (G1SimNode.h:414, g1_sim.yaml:24), which this direct model load does not apply

the G1 actuator block sets no ctrlrange, so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound; the package declares no bound of its own and the joint actuatorfrcrange values are not used as ctrl limits

cap.world.seed.v1 is not served because the MuJoCo bridge has no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults; the upstream ROS simulator's command topics, services, elastic band, monitor stream and FSM state switching are out of scope for this direct model driver
the second and third card models (the Tron1A scene and the G1 robot include) are not separately served; the card's first scene is the served model

no physical humanoid is modelled and nothing was validated against Unitree G1 hardware; the repository's crl_humanoid_hardware nodes for the real G1 (Unitree SDK2) and Tron1A (LimX SDK) are out of scope; only the simulated world state and the derived control vector are exposed

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the MuJoCo integration state is kept and stays readable
